bull.b: Sustained revenue scaling together with a multi-year gross margin improvement implies stronger pricing, better mix and operating leverage. These structural trends support durable operating cash flow expansion and provide room to invest in distribution or product breadth over the next 2–6 months.

bull.t: Steady cash generation and improving FCF
bull.b: Consistent operating cash flow and a meaningful improvement in free cash flow in 2025 indicate the business converts revenue into cash reliably. That persistent cash generation underpins debt servicing, capex and strategic investments, increasing financial resilience over the medium term.

The completed refinancing replaces near-term maturities with longer-dated secured notes and a 2033 term loan, reducing near-term refinancing pressure. Extending maturities and consolidating facilities materially improves liquidity runway and gives management time to delever or execute strategy.

bear.b: Leverage around or above 1x equity materially constrains flexibility: higher interest and covenant exposure reduce capacity for opportunistic investment, increase refinancing sensitivity, and can amplify earnings pressure if sales or margins weaken over the coming months.

bear.t: Margin volatility and net margin compression
bear.b: Despite gross margin gains, net and operating margins have shown volatility and recent compression, indicating cost or SG&A pressures. Persistent volatility means revenue growth may not reliably translate to profit, complicating forecasting and limiting sustainable free cash flow expansion.

bear.t: COO retirement and operations leadership risk
bear.b: A planned COO departure for health reasons creates a leadership transition during a period of active refinancing and operational execution. Replacing operational leadership risks short-term continuity in supply chain, margin initiatives and integration projects, and could slow implementation of strategic plans.
